blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Looped transformers increase effective depth by repeatedly applying a shared set of transformer layers, offering a parameter-efficient way to scale computation. However, standard residual connections aggregate information across recurrent depth into a single stream, providing limited control over which intermediate representations from preceding layers should be reused. In this paper, we introduce ARLoop, a looped transformer architecture based on attention residuals, where the input of each layer is selectively aggregated through attention over model depth. Distinct from standard transformers, we find that looped transformers do not require access to the full residual history: sliding-window depth attention matches or outperforms full-history attention at larger recurrent depths. Across controlled experiments with multiple parameter scales (140M and 370M) and recurrent depths (R = 1 to 5), ARLoop consistently outperforms prior residual designs for looped transformers. More importantly, we further scale ARLoop to 0.6B and 1.2B parameters under a realistic LLM pretraining recipe, demonstrating that the gains transfer to realistic pretraining, with particularly strong improvements on math and coding tasks. Our 1.2B model, pretrained on only 0.5T tokens with three recurrences, outperforms Huginn-3.5B (the only fully-open looped LLM as of our release date) across all evaluated tasks and is competitive with similar-sized non-looped models such as Qwen3.5-2B despite being trained on substantially less data.
blocks.zh: 环绕式变压器通过反复应用一组共享的变压器层来提高有效深度,提供了一个参数高效的计算方法. 然而,标准残余连接将跨经常性深度的信息汇总到单一流中,对前几层的中间表述应当重新使用的控制有限。 在本文中,我们引入了ARLoop,一种基于注意力残留的环绕式变压器架构,其中每个层的输入通过注意力在模型深度上选择性地聚合. 与标准变压器不同,我们发现环绕变压器不需要访问完整的剩余历史:滑动-窗口深度注意力匹配或者在更大的重复深度中超越了全历史注意力. 纵观多参数尺度(140M和370M)和重复深度(R=1至5)的受控实验,ARLoop在环绕变压器的先前剩余设计上一直表现优于. 更重要的是,我们在现实的LLM预训配方下,进一步将ARLoop的参数扩大至0.6B和1.2B,表明收益转移至现实的预训,在数学和编码任务方面有特别强的改进. 我们的1.2B模型,只预先训练了0.5T令牌,有三次重现,超过Huginn-3.5B(截至我们发布之日唯一完全开放的LLM),在所有评估任务上,尽管接受的数据少得多的培训,却与类似大小的非Lood模型,如Qune3.5-2B,具有竞争力.

blocks.en:
Looped transformers repeatedly apply a small set of shared transformer layers,
increasing effective depth without increasing the number of distinct parameters ( Dehghani et al., 2019 ; Yang et al., 2024 ; Saunshi et al., 2025 ) .
This provides an appealing alternative to conventional depth scaling:
the same parameters can be reused for additional computation,
and the number of recurrences provides an explicit axis along which
training and inference compute can be varied.
Recent work has demonstrated that such models can improve
generalization on controlled multi-hop reasoning tasks ( Kohli et al., 2026 ) .
Meanwhile, growing interest has focused on scaling looped transformers
for parameter-efficient pretraining of large language models (LLMs) ( Geiping et al., 2025 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ) .
A central question, however, is how to make looped transformers effectively exploit the additional computation provided by recurrent depth .

blocks.en:
Increasing recurrent depth repeatedly produces new intermediate representations,
but standard transformer residual connections, such as PreNorm ( Xiong et al., 2020 ) ,
provide only a limited mechanism for controlling how information produced
at earlier depths is reused.
Under PreNorm, residual updates from previous depths are accumulated
into a single residual stream with fixed unit coefficients.
As recurrence increases, more updates are accumulated into the same state,
while later computations have no explicit mechanism for selecting
which representations produced at earlier depths are useful.
Existing work has improved looped transformers through residual scaling
or normalization ( Geiping et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2026 ; Prairie et al., 2026 ) ,
but limited systematic comparisons leave it unclear which residual design best enables models
to make use of recurrent computation.
Moreover, these prior residual designs have mostly been evaluated under
relatively small-scale pretraining setups, leaving their effectiveness
on more complex generative tasks such as mathematical reasoning and
code generation underexplored.

blocks.en:
Motivated by recent advances in attention residuals for standard transformers ( Kimi Team, 2026 ) ,
we investigate how selective residual access should be adapted to recurrent depth.
Compared with PreNorm, attention residuals replace the uniform aggregation
of earlier residual updates with attention-weighted aggregation,
allowing each layer to selectively access representations from preceding depths.
Unlike standard transformers, however, recurrent depth repeatedly applies
the same parameters
and can produce highly redundant representations
across recurrences ( Zeitoun et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026a ) , raising the question of whether access to the full
residual history is necessary.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are twofold.
First, we introduce ARLoop , a looped transformer architecture
that adapts attention residuals to recurrent depth.
Across multiple parameter scales (140M and 370M) and recurrence depths
( R = 1 R=1 to R = 5 R=5 ), ARLoop consistently improves validation perplexity
over PreNorm and outperforms prior residual designs ( Geiping et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2026 ; Prairie et al., 2026 ) under our rigorous controlled evaluation setting.
Distinct from standard transformers, we find that access to the full residual
history is unnecessary for looped transformers:
sliding-window depth attention matches or outperforms full-history attention
at larger recurrence depths.
Our analysis further shows that depth attention concentrates on recent
residual sources and that representations across recurrences are highly
redundant, explaining the effectiveness of sliding-window attention.

blocks.en:
More importantly, we demonstrate that ARLoop scales to work under a realistic LLM pretraining recipe.
Despite using a much smaller training budget (i.e. 0.5T tokens), our strongest ARLoop-1.2B substantially outperforms
Huginn-3.5B ( Geiping et al., 2025 ) (the only fully-open looped LLM as of our release date), and achieves performance competitive with strong non-looped LLMs such as Qwen3.5-2B.
At scale, we find that ARLoop generally outperforms PreNorm, with especially promising improvements on math and coding tasks (e.g. +5.2 points on GSM8K and +3.1 points on MBPP).
We release training code and checkpoints, making ARLoop fully-open for future study.

在规模上,我们发现ARLoop一般优于PreNorm,在数学和编码任务上特别有希望的改进(如GSM8K上+5.2分和MBPP上+3.1分).
我们公布训练守则和检查站,使ARLOOP完全开放供今后研究。

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Looped transformers, also known as recurrent-depth transformers or universal transformers ( Dehghani et al., 2019 ; Lan et al., 2020 ; Yang et al., 2024 ) , are widely studied as memory-efficient alternatives to transformers.
As they are increasingly scaled to LLM pretraining ( Csordás et al., 2024 ; Geiping et al., 2025 ; Bae et al., 2025 ) , recent work has explored residual designs for better information propagation across recurrent depth, including Parcae, DeepLoop, and HyperLoop ( Li et al., 2026 ; Zeitoun et al., 2026 ; Prairie et al., 2026 ; Knupp et al., 2026 ) .
Compared with these approaches, ARLoop consistently matches or outperforms them across parameter and recurrence budgets in our controlled experiments. We further show that these gains extend beyond language modeling perplexity to mathematical reasoning and code generation, which remain underexplored in prior work.

环形变流器又称相通式深度变流器或通用变流器(德赫干尼等,2019;兰等,2020;杨等,2024)被广泛研究为变流器的内存高效替代品.
随着它们日益被扩大为LLM预训(Csordás等人,2024;Geiping等人,2025;Bae等人,2025;),最近的工作探索了残余设计,以便更好地在经常深度传播信息,包括Parcae、DeepLoop和HyperLoop(Li等人,2026;Zeitoun等人,2026;Prairie等人,2026;Knupp等人,2026;)。
与这些方法相比,ARLoop在我们所控制的实验中,在参数和重复预算方面始终比对或超过它们。 我们进一步表明,这些成果超越了语言模型的模糊性,而扩展到数学推理和代码生成,而数学推理和代码生成在以前的工作中仍然没有得到充分利用。

blocks.en:
Recent work has begun scaling looped transformers for pretraining. Geiping et al. (2025) introduced Huginn, a 3.5B-parameter looped LLM trained with up to 64 recurrences, while Zhu et al. (2025) further scaled the training data with Ouro, a 1.4B model using up to four recurrences.
Subsequent work has explored looped LLMs with mixture-of-experts architectures such as Loopies ( Gao et al., 2026 ) , SMELT ( Wang et al., 2026b ) , as well as larger data scales for advanced capabilities, including Nanbeige4.2-3B ( Lab et al., 2026 ) and LoopCoder-v2 ( Yang et al., 2026 ) .
Despite these promising results, many looped LLMs release only model weights
or do not release weights at all, leaving the training and data recipe unclear.
The only exception is Huginn, which releases all training artifacts.
In particular, Huginn reports that PreNorm does not effectively exploit recurrent depth and instead relies on conservative optimization setups for stable training.
Our work systematically studies residual design for looped transformers and further validates the resulting architecture under a realistic LLM pretraining recipe, substantially outperforming Huginn despite using smaller parameter, data, and recurrence budgets.

Since attention residuals only change how each sublayer aggregates representations
from preceding depths, they can be naturally applied to looped transformers.
Figure 2 a illustrates a simplified example in which
each recurrence contains two sublayers.
As the depth grows, residual updates are grouped into one or more residual
blocks following Equation 4 .
Each effective sublayer has its own learned query vector
(i.e. q i q_{i} in Figure 2 b),
which attends over the residual sources available at that depth.
Compared with PreNorm-based looped transformers, this allows sublayers at
deeper recurrences to selectively access representations produced at earlier
recurrent depths.

Standard attention residuals allow each depth-attention operation to access
all preceding residual blocks as candidate sources, which we refer to as full-history depth attention .
In a looped transformer, however, the same set of parameters is
repeatedly applied across recurrences, potentially introducing redundancy among
representations produced at different recurrent depths.
Indeed, prior work has observed high similarity between hidden states across
recurrences in looped transformers ( Zeitoun et al., 2026 ) .
This motivates us to ask whether access to the full residual history is necessary,
or whether recent residual states already provide sufficient information.

where b 0 b_{0} denotes the input embedding and b m b_{m} is the most recent residual block.
Given a window size W W , sliding-window depth attention restricts the source set to ℬ W = { b 0 , b max ⁡ ( 1 , m − W + 1 ) , … , b m } . \mathcal{B}_{W}=\{b_{0},b_{\max(1,m-W+1)},\ldots,b_{m}\}. Thus, the input embedding remains directly accessible at every depth,

sliding-window depth attention can match and even outperform full-history
attention in looped transformers, particularly at larger recurrence depths.

blocks.en: We first use controlled experiments to evaluate how effectively ARLoop reuses information across recurrent depth, examining both its benefits for language modeling and the contribution of its key design choices.

Following Prairie et al. (2026) , we pretrain these models

respectively, with a context length of 2048.
Following the general architecture of Karpathy (2025) , each transformer layer uses
multi-head attention and a standard MLP.
For optimization, we use AdamW ( Kingma and Ba, 2017 ) with a cosine learning rate schedule.
Complete architecture and training details are provided in Appendix A.1 .

blocks.en: 5 Scaling to Practical Pretraining of Looped Transformers
blocks.zh: 5 扩大循环变换器的实用预训

blocks.en: Having established the effectiveness of ARLoop in controlled experiments, we now scale it to billion-parameter models, bringing together carefully curated pretraining data mixtures and a multi-stage training strategy to build strong, fully-open ARLoop -based LLMs.
blocks.zh: 在确定了ARLoop在受控实验中的有效性之后,我们现在将其扩大为十亿参数模型,将精心整理的预培训数据混合物和多阶段培训战略结合起来,以建立强大、完全开放的ARLoop-基于LLMs。

blocks.en:
We adopt a pretraining recipe similar to SmolLM ( Allal et al., 2025 ; HuggingFaceTB, 2025 ) .
Compared with the controlled experiments in Section 4 ,
we replace multi-head attention with grouped-query attention ( Ainslie et al., 2023 ) and use SwiGLU ( Shazeer, 2020 ) in place of the standard FFN sublayers to better align with modern LLM architectures ( Qwen Team, 2025 ) .
For pretraining data, we use FineWeb-Edu ( Penedo et al., 2024 ) , FineMath, and Stack-Edu ( Allal et al., 2025 ) as the primary sources.
We use the same cosine learning rate schedule and adopt a multi-stage training
strategy, introducing higher-quality data in later stages following HuggingFaceTB (2025) and Allen Institute for AI (2025) .
We also extend the context length to 4096 tokens.
Such a realistic pretraining recipe enables us to evaluate our models not only on general knowledge and reasoning tasks, but also on mathematical reasoning and code generation.
We provide complete architecture, training, and data-mixture details in
Appendix B.1 .

blocks.en:
Using this recipe, we train three models:
(1) PreNormLoop-0.6B , a 0.6B PreNormLoop model with 18 transformer layers and R = 3 R=3 , trained on 180B tokens;
(2) ARLoop-0.6B , a 0.6B ARLoop model with the same architecture, recurrence, and training budget; and
(3) ARLoop-1.2B , a 1.2B ARLoop model with 24 transformer layers and R = 3 R=3 , trained on 500B tokens.
For both ARLoop models, we adopt the sliding-window configuration from Section 4 .

We additionally compare against both existing looped language models
and strong non-looped LLMs of similar or larger sizes.
The recurrent-depth baselines include Huginn ( Geiping et al., 2025 ) and Ouro ( Zhu et al., 2025 ) ,
while the non-looped open models include Qwen3.5-2B ( Qwen Team, 2026 ) ,
Gemma 3-4B ( Gemma Team, 2025 ) ,
OLMo 2-7B and OLMo 3-7B ( Team OLMo et al., 2024 ; Allen Institute for AI, 2025 ) .
The non-looped open models are included mainly as references rather than for head-to-head comparison.
For all of these models, we re-evaluate the corresponding base checkpoints
using the same evaluation harness to ensure consistent evaluation.
Among these models,
we particularly focus on Huginn because it is a fully-open looped LLM trained with a comparable data scale, but with substantially larger parameter and recurrence budgets (e.g. 3.5B parameters and up to 64 recurrences).

blocks.en:
Note that we do not compare with other residual methods such as Parcae or DeepLoop ( Prairie et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026 ; Zeitoun et al., 2026 ) in this realistic pretraining comparison.
Such previous work generally validates their methods only at small data scales (e.g. below 50B tokens) or with a single pretraining source (e.g. FineWeb-Edu), leaving the capabilities of the resulting models on more complex tasks such as math and coding open.
Our contribution specifically targets this question, aiming to show ARLoop remains effective on such generative tasks under realistic pretraining settings.

blocks.en: 5.1 Results
blocks.zh: 5.1 结果

blocks.en:
Table 3 reports our large-scale training results.
Under the same 0.6B parameter scale, 180B-token training budget, and R = 3 R=3 recurrence, ARLoop-0.6B outperforms PreNormLoop-0.6B on 7 of 8 evaluated tasks.
The gains are particularly large on mathematical reasoning and code generation,
including +5.2 points on GSM8K and +3.1 points on MBPP.
These results suggest that the benefits of ARLoop indeed transfer to a realistic LLM pretraining recipe.
Interestingly, while the gains in validation perplexity are relatively modest in
the controlled experiments, they become substantially larger on complex generative tasks.
This highlights the importance of evaluating residual designs beyond perplexity
and multiple-choice benchmarks, which is missing in existing work ( Prairie et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026 ; Zeitoun et al., 2026 ) .

Scaling ARLoop to 1.2B parameters and 500B training tokens yields substantial improvements across all evaluated benchmarks.
In particular, ARLoop-1.2B outperforms Huginn on every task in Table 3 ,
despite using fewer parameters, fewer training tokens, and substantially fewer recurrent steps.
Although ARLoop-1.2B underperforms Ouro ( Zhu et al., 2025 ) on most tasks,
we attribute this gap primarily to their substantially larger pretraining data budget and its use of higher-quality pretraining data sources.
Instead, our training recipe relies on open and commonly used data sources.
Our model is also competitive with Qwen3.5-2B despite its substantially smaller pretraining budget,
matching or exceeding it on all evaluated benchmarks. ARLoop-1.2B also outperforms
Gemma-3-4B on both math benchmarks and OLMo models on HumanEval,
demonstrating competitive math and coding capabilities
against substantially larger non-looped LLMs.
These results show that attention residuals can substantially strengthen looped LLMs,
making them competitive with strong non-looped LLMs at similar parameter scales.

blocks.en:
To better understand the gains of ARLoop on math and coding tasks, we adopt the layer effect metric from Csordás et al. (2025) to quantify how much each layer contributes to representations at subsequent layers.
We randomly sample 50 examples from MATH and, for each example, intervene on the representation of a source layer and measure the resulting change in the outputs of deeper layers.
Figure 4 compares the layer effects between PreNormLoop-0.6B and ARLoop-0.6B .
We find that layers in the second and third recurrences of ARLoop make substantially larger contributions to subsequent layers than the corresponding deeper layers in PreNormLoop-0.6B .
This suggests that ARLoop makes greater use of representations computed at later recurrent depths, consistent with its stronger performance on tasks that benefit from deeper computation.
We report the detailed score computation and results on MBPP in Appendix C .

blocks.en: 6 Further discussion
blocks.zh: 6 进一步讨论

blocks.en:
Existing looped language models often vary the number of recurrences during training
to support multiple effective depths ( Geiping et al., 2025 ; Prairie et al., 2026 ; Kohli et al., 2026 ; Bae et al., 2025 ) .
We compare such dynamic-recurrence training with fixed R = 4 R=4 training and find
that fixed recurrence consistently achieves better validation perplexity and
downstream performance at both the 140M and 370M scales.
We therefore use fixed recurrence in our main experiments.
Complete training setups and results are provided in
Appendix D.1 .

blocks.en:
We also investigate whether the improved residual access of ARLoop enables inference-time recurrence extrapolation, i.e. benefiting from more
recurrences than observed during training ( Fan et al., 2025 ; Kohli et al., 2026 ) .
Consistent with prior observations for looped language models ( Prairie et al., 2026 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ) ,
we find that performance improves up to the maximum training recurrence but
does not further improve beyond it.
This suggests that selective access to earlier representations alone does not
unlock recurrence extrapolation: effectively composing information within the
trained depth range and generalizing recurrent computation beyond that range
appear to be distinct problems.
Complete experimental details are provided in
Appendix D.2 .

blocks.en:
ARLoop introduces additional computation due to the attention residual calculation for each sublayer.
When activation checkpointing (e.g. recomputation of intermediate hidden states) is not enabled, the residual sources used by attention residual are already retained for backpropagation, resulting in negligible additional memory overhead.
We report training memory and throughput for our experimental setups in Table 4 .
Across all model scales, ARLoop uses essentially the same amount of memory as PreNorm.
In terms of throughput, ARLoop full is approximately 15% slower than PreNorm on average, while sliding window attention residual reduces this gap to approximately 10%.
We expect that further kernel optimization could reduce this overhead, as depth attention introduces relatively little additional arithmetic computation but incurs additional high-bandwidth memory traffic.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We introduce ARLoop , a looped transformer architecture that adapts attention residuals to recurrent depth.
Through controlled experiments across multiple parameter scales, ARLoop consistently outperforms PreNorm and prior residual designs for looped transformers.
Distinct from standard transformers, we find that looped transformers do not require access to the full residual history: sliding-window depth attention can match or outperform full-history attention at larger recurrence depths.
More importantly, we demonstrate that these gains transfer to realistic LLM pretraining.
At the 0.6B scale, ARLoop substantially improves over a matched PreNorm model, with particularly large gains on math and coding tasks.
Our strongest model ARLoop-1.2B substantially outperforms the fully-open looped LLM Huginn and is competitive with Qwen3.5-2B despite being trained on substantially less data.
Together, these results demonstrate that selective residual access provides an effective way for looped transformers to better exploit recurrent computation at scale.
blocks.zh:
我们引入了 ARLOOP,一个循环变压器架构 使注意力的剩余 适应反复出现的深度。
通过跨多参数尺度的受控实验,ARLooPerNorm和前作的环绕变压器剩余设计一直比性能高.
与标准变压器不同,我们发现环绕变压器不需要访问完整的剩余历史:滑动-窗口深度关注可以在更大的重现深度中匹配或超过全历史关注.
更重要的是,我们表明,这些收益转移到现实的LLM预训。
在0.6B尺度上,ARLoop大大改进了相匹配的PreNorm模型,在数学和编码任务上特别大的进展.
我们最强的ARLoop-1.2B型车的性能大大超过完全开通的LLM Huginn型机车,并且虽然在数据方面受到的训练要少得多,却与Quen3.5-2B型机车具有竞争力.
这些结果表明,选择性的剩余访问为循环式变压器提供了一个有效途径,以更好地利用规模的经常性计算。

blocks.en: A.1 Architecture and Training.

blocks.en:
Table 5 specifies the 140M and 370M model families used in Section 4 .
The table describes the shared backbone of PreNorm, ARLoop full , and ARLoop sw . Each recurrence reuses the entire physical layer stack; increasing R R increases the effective depth without adding Transformer layers.
Depth-attention queries and normalization parameters are specific to each effective sublayer.
At the final effective depth, we apply a separate attention-residual aggregation to produce the representation passed to the language modeling head.
We use a scaled-zero initialization, which is the same strategy as Prairie et al. (2026) .
The additional baselines retain the same model dimensions and use their respective residual updates and initialization rules.
blocks.zh:
表5列出了第4节中使用的140M和370M模式家庭。
该表描述了PreNorm、ARLoop full和ARLoop sw的共享骨干。 每次重现都会再用整个物理地层堆栈;增加R会增加有效深度而不会增加变形器地层.
深度关注询问和常态化参数是每个有效子层所特有的.
在最后有效的深度,我们采用单独的关注-剩余汇总方法来制作传给语文建模主管的表述。
我们使用一个规模零初始化,这是与Prairie等人(2026年)相同的策略.
额外的基线保留了相同的模型维度并使用了各自的剩余更新和初始化规则.

blocks.en:
Following the default setup of Karpathy (2025) , we use value residuals ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) in all experiments.
Specifically, at alternating effective layers (e.g., the 1st, 3rd, and 5th layers), we inject a gated token embedding into the value vectors of the self-attention sublayer.
These token-specific embedding parameters are distinct from the input embeddings.
Value residual learning has been shown to improve LLM pretraining ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) and has also been adopted in recent looped-transformer architectures ( Prairie et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh:
继"Karopathy"(2025)的默认设置后,我们在所有实验中使用了价值残值(周等,2025年).
具体地说,在交替有效地层(例如第一,第三,第五地层)中,我们注入了嵌入自意子层的值向量的有门的活性符.
这些特定符号的嵌入参数与输入嵌入有区别.
价值剩余学习已被证明可以改进LLM预训(周等,2025年),并被采用于近代循环-转录建筑(Prairie等,2026年).

blocks.en:
Although value residuals are not a contribution of our work, we find them important for obtaining strong looped-transformer performance, particularly at smaller scales.
Importantly, removing value residuals substantially degrades our sliding-window depth-attention variant.
They are even more important for Sandwich-Norm looped transformers: without value residuals, training becomes unstable and the loss remains near 7.5 rather than continuing to decrease.
This pattern is consistent with the failed Sandwich-Norm training run reported by Geiping et al. (2025, Figure 5, Bad Run 1) .
We hypothesize that this instability is related to representation collapse at large effective depths, where representations of different tokens become increasingly similar, and
repeated injection of token-specific information through value residuals mitigates this effect.
Empirically, adding value residuals eliminates the observed training failure and makes the Sandwich-Norm variant trainable in our setting.
blocks.zh:
尽管剩余价值不是我们工作的贡献,但我们认为它们对于获得强有力的循环转换性能,特别是在较小的尺度上,是重要的。
重要的是,去除价值残值会大大地降低我们的滑窗深度观察变体。
对桑威奇-诺姆环形变压器来说,它们更为重要:没有剩余价值,培训就变得不稳定,损失仍然接近7.5,而不是继续减少。

As shown in Table 9 , sliding-window depth attention slightly improves the looped model, whereas directly applying the same window to the non-recurrent transformer substantially degrades performance.
To better understand this difference, we further visualize the pairwise cosine similarity between residual blocks in the non-recurrent model in Figure 6 .
The non-recurrent transformer exhibits a markedly different pattern from the looped models, with substantially lower similarity across residual blocks.
This suggests that distinct depths in standard transformers contain less redundant representations, consistent with our hypothesis that the high redundancy across recurrences in looped transformers makes sliding-window depth attention particularly well suited to their recurrent-depth structure.

blocks.en: A.6 The effect of residual block and sliding window sizes

blocks.en:
We additionally study the effect of residual block size, i.e. the number of sublayers contained in each residual block, and sliding-window size, i.e. the number of recent residual blocks retained by sliding-window depth attention.
We primarily use the 140M ARLoop for these studies.

我们进一步研究残余区块大小的影响,即每个残余区块所包含子层的数量,以及滑行-窗口大小,即通过滑行-窗口深度关注保留了最近残余区块的数量.
我们主要使用140MARLOOP进行这些研究.

blocks.en:
Table 10 reports the validation perplexities of models trained with different residual block sizes across recurrence settings.
We find that using finer-grained residual blocks (i.e. smaller block sizes) does not consistently improve validation perplexity.
While finer-grained blocks are beneficial for non-recurrent transformers, consistent with Kimi Team (2026) , we find that their benefit diminishes as the number of recurrences increases, and smaller blocks can even hurt performance at larger R R .
We hypothesize that this is related to the same phenomenon observed in Section 4.1 : residual-block representations are highly redundant across recurrences, and using smaller blocks introduces more residual sources from earlier recurrences, potentially further increasing this redundancy.
blocks.zh:
表10报告在重复设置中以不同残块大小培训的模型的验证难度。

虽然更细纹的块对非经常性变压器有益,但与Kimi Team(2026)一致,我们发现它们的好处会随着重现次数的增加而减少,更小的块甚至会伤害更大的R R的性能.
我们假设这与第4.1节所观察到的同样现象有关:残余区块表示在重复发生时非常重复,使用较小的区块引入了更早重复出现的残余来源,有可能使这种重复增加。

blocks.en:
We evaluate the per-sequence Poisson model described above at each recurrence R = 1 , … , 8 R=1,\ldots,8 , using the same validation set as in Section 4 .
During training, the recurrence is bounded by R ≤ 4 R\leq 4 ; evaluation at R > 4 R>4 therefore requires computation at effective depths that are never
encountered during the original training.
Since our attention-residual mechanism uses a learned query for each
effective sublayer, evaluating beyond the maximum training recurrence
introduces queries at previously unseen depths.
We randomly initialize these additional queries and train only their
parameters on an additional 0.5B FineWeb-Edu tokens, while freezing all
other model parameters.
This provides a favorable setting for recurrence extrapolation: rather
than requiring the model to reuse or extrapolate query parameters to
unseen depths, the newly introduced queries are explicitly optimized to
aggregate the residual history available at those depths.

blocks.en:
We train our models on NVIDIA A100 80GB, H100, and B200 GPUs.
The controlled experiments require approximately 12K GPU hours in total, including early-stage exploration.
Pretraining the PreNormLoop-0.6B and ARLoop-0.6B models takes approximately one week on 8 H100 GPUs.
The ARLoop-1.2B model is trained on 16 B200 GPUs for approximately two weeks.
